newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Shooting breaks out at Korean border.
newsitem.headline: Shooting breaks out at Korean border.

text.p: North and South Korean soldiers exchanged fire at the border on Wednesday, a Southern defence ministry official said, raising tensions as the two Koreas prepare for peace talks.
"There was an exchange of fire between South and North Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone this morning," said the official, asking not to be identified.
There were no reports of casualties.

"The shooting broke out after a group of North Korean soldiers crossed the Military Demarcation Line in the western sector of the frontier at around 10.50 a.m. (0150 GMT). They returned to the north at around noon," he said.

The Military Demarcation Line runs midway through the four-km (2.5-mile) wide DMZ that bisects the peninsula. A ministry spokesman said details of the incident were being pieced together and an announcement would be made later on Wednesday.
Yonhap Television News said the North Korean soldiers ignored repeated broadcast warnings and began shooting at a southern guard post. South Korean troops returned fire from the guard post.

The shooting took place only three weeks before the two Koreas, the United States and China were due to hold talks to pave the way for negotiations aimed at thrashing out a peace treaty to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
Senior officials from the four nations are due to meet in New York on August 5 to set an agenda and other procedural details for the peace talks.
The DMZ was set up as a buffer zone at the end of the war, but is now one of the world's most heavily fortified frontiers.
In April, North and South Korean troops exchanged warning shots at the DMZ shortly before visiting U.S. defence Secretary William Cohen flew to the area.
